proof_attempt_summary: Derived the explicit fixed-channel n^-4/3 deficit order for the true realized contrast against arbitrary outcome-independent dependent assignments and full-record estimator kernels; broadened the general scope to fixed K≥2 and proved a strict finite label-value witness. Mathematics and citation checks passed, but the specialized extension, loose constants, conservative threshold, and lack of broad finite-sample optimality cap the package at subfield under the projected-score gate. No Lean formalization was run; sharp coefficients and broader finite-sample optimality remain prospective contribution-level work.
tldr: For every fixed \(K\ge2\), every nonzero real zero-sum contrast and fixed known symmetric channels with positive active accuracies, the unrestricted true finite-population minimax risk is \(C_\kappa/n-\Theta_{c,\kappa}(n^{-4/3})\), where \(C_\kappa=(\sum_{a\in S}|c_a|/\kappa_a)^2/4\). Independent allocation \(q_a^\star\propto|c_a|/\kappa_a\) and a total projected clipped-score rule give an explicit positive gain. A channel-aligned prior on complete true schedules gives the matching deficit order against every outcome-independent assignment law, including dependent designs, and every full-record estimator kernel. The converse retains the arm-labelled conditional realized target. A channel-convolved orbit/grid program gives finite risk certificates. In the specialized three-arm, three-subject example, \(V_3^{\mathrm{full}}\le1581/4096<27/56\le V_3^{\mathrm{sign}}\) certifies a strict finite value from retaining labels; the exact full-record value remains undetermined.
gap: The verified clean finite-population results establish nonlinear second-order gains, while noisy causal estimation and misclassification-aware allocation are established in other decision problems. Those results do not certify the full-record converse for the supplied heterogeneous-channel experiment and the realized true contrast.
fill: The main theorem combines an adapted finite-alphabet upper argument with a true-schedule Bayes lower bound, explicit positive constants and a finite threshold. Finite orbit likelihoods preserve labels and provide a checkable program for the same loss.
